overview.description: Every component has a hand-authored <name>.contract.json meant to be a machine-readable contract (props, anatomy, tokens, a11y, behavior rules). An audit found severe shape inconsistency across the 28 files - not just missing fields, but genuinely incompatible JSON shapes for the same field name. docs/components/registry.json is generated from these files by scripts/generate-component-registry.mjs, which normalizes every field to one canonical shape and validates the result against docs/foundations/component-registry.schema.json. This is the reliable, single-fetch, machine-consumable view; the source contract.json files remain the deep-dive reference for one component's full, un-normalized detail.
overview.purpose: Let an agent or tool query structural facts (props, anatomy, sizes, slots, variants) across many components at once without reading 28 differently-shaped files, while never fabricating content the source files don't actually contain.

rawShapesHandled: object keyed by group -> array of strings (flattened, group preserved on each entry)
object keyed by part -> description string ({name: key, description: value})
normalizationRules.dataDropped: Button-style per-part {element, required} detail is not carried into the registry - read the source contract.json for that.
none - missing sub-fields become null/false, never a fabricated value

rawShapesHandled: object keyed by size name -> dimension detail (reduced to Object.keys())
absent - see the sizingDetail escape hatch below for the Skeleton-style free-size case
normalizationRules.dataDropped: per-size token/dimension detail (e.g. exact height/padding/radius per size) - read the source contract.json for that.

normalizationRules.canonicalShape: passthrough object, only present when the source file has a `sizing` key and no `sizes` key
normalizationRules.note: Free-size components (e.g. Skeleton) don't have a size enum - detected structurally (has sizing, lacks sizes), not by component name, so a future component reusing this pattern is handled automatically.

normalizationRules.dataDropped: per-slot supports/interactive detail - read the source contract.json for that.

rawShapesHandled: axis -> object of arbitrary per-value detail
mixed shapes across a single file's own axes (dispatched per-axis, not per-file)
normalizationRules.dataDropped: per-variant purpose/className/dimension detail - read the source contract.json for that.

normalizationRules.canonicalShape: Array<{name, anatomy, props}>, always present ([] when unused)
normalizationRules.note: Handles the Radio contract.json, which documents Radio and RadioGroup in one file (no top-level anatomy/props, nested under radio/radioGroup keys instead). Detected structurally so a future multi-component file is handled the same way.

contentCompleteness.description: Each registry entry gets a structurally-derived contentCompleteness: full | partial | stub, based on how many of 8 near-universal substantive sections (purpose, useCases, states, accessibility, behaviorRules, do, dont, acceptanceCriteria) are present and non-empty in the source file.
contentCompleteness.purpose: Surfaces real content gaps (not shape drift) as a queryable signal instead of only living in prose a reader might skip.

knownContentGaps.issue: 4 top-level keys only (name, anatomy, props, tokens) - missing purpose, useCases, states, accessibility, behaviorRules, do/dont, acceptanceCriteria entirely.
knownContentGaps.resolution: Author the missing sections from the real avatar.tsx behavior next time Avatar is substantively touched. Not something the registry generator can or should paper over - filling this in requires real component analysis, not normalization.

knownContentGaps.issue: 11 top-level keys - missing useCases, props (!), sizes, slots, do/dont, acceptanceCriteria.
knownContentGaps.resolution: Same as Avatar - author when next substantively touched.

knownContentGaps.issue: 12 top-level keys - missing tokens entirely, plus useCases, do/dont, acceptanceCriteria.
knownContentGaps.resolution: Same as Avatar - author when next substantively touched.

knownShapeDrift.description: Contract.json files authored before this normalization convention existed may use any of the rawShapesHandled variants documented above per field. This is expected and handled automatically by the generator - it is not a per-file violations ledger (roughly 24 of 28 files deviate from a single canonical shape in at least one field, which would make an enumerated list unwieldy and low-value).
knownShapeDrift.resolution: When a component's contract.json is next substantively touched, converge its anatomy/props/sizes/slots/variants directly to the canonical shapes documented above, reducing reliance on generator-side normalization over time. Same 'migrate when next touched' philosophy as component-api-governance.json's knownViolations for Button/IconButton's isDisabled prop - applied at the shape level instead of enumerated per file.

validationApproach.rationale: One source of truth (component-registry.schema.json) instead of a second hardcoded shadow-copy of the shape in validator code. No new runtime dependency, consistent with this repo's narrowly-scoped-tooling precedent (stylelint-declaration-strict-value is a single-purpose plugin, not a general rule engine).
validationApproach.revisitThreshold: Add a real JSON Schema library (e.g. ajv) only if the schema needs features the mini-interpreter doesn't support (oneOf, $ref, conditional if/then) - not before. This is a conscious future decision point, not something to reach for preemptively.

generation.rationale: docs/components/registry.json is committed generated output, colocated with its source data - same convention as packages/ui/src/tokens/generated (Style Dictionary build output, also committed, not gitignored). Not wired into `npm run validate` or CI, matching the existing npm run generate:icons precedent (also a manual, on-demand command, not auto-run or staleness-checked in CI).
